searchText: Are there any efforts to write a tool which keeps track of the ETH supply? With the upcoming hardfork & withdrawals, it will not be accurate for existing services i saw erigons flag > There is an optional stage that can be enabled through flags: > --watch-the-burn, Enable WatchTheBurn stage which keeps track of ETH issuance and is required to use erigon_watchTheBurn. will this be updated? cc <@552133098075193354> Good question! I can look into it. cc: <@687974325072035882> Okay I can take a look at it Although post merge it does not keep track of newly issue CL ethers It estimates to be block rewards to be 0.3 eth as an approximation So it is not exact anymore but just an approximation. However when Erigon will have an embedded full CL this may be changed thanks!! Where did we land wrt specifying timestamp-based forks? <@360491619402776577> IIRC you said a while back you'd draft an EIP once all clients had an implementation. Is that still necessary you think? I have an eip "ready" It's a draft on the eip repo Are clients happy with this schema for withdrawals on the json-rpc? https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/334
